title: Identify security, safety and environmental risks in the local environment

lessons.title: Safety risks around you
lessons.html:
What is a risk?

A hazard is something that can hurt you, like a moving auger or a slippery floor. A risk is the chance that it will hurt someone. On a farm, at a silo or in a grain store there are many hazards. If you learn to see them, you can stay safe and keep others safe.

Common safety hazards at work

HazardWhat can happen
Moving machines: augers, conveyors, belts, tractorsClothes or hands get pulled in; people get run over
Grain bins and silosA person sinks in grain and cannot breathe
Grain dustBreathing problems; dust can burn or explode
Heavy bagsBack injuries; falling stacks
Chemicals and poisonsBurns, poisoning
Heights: ladders, truck topsFalls
ElectricityShock, burns, fire

What you must do

  • Wear your safety shoes, overalls, gloves and dust mask.
  • Keep away from moving parts. Never take off a guard.
  • Never go into a bin or silo unless you are trained and have permission.
  • Do not smoke near grain, fuel or chemicals.
  • Keep walkways clean. Sweep up spilled grain.
  • Lift with your legs, not your back.

Report it

If you see something unsafe, tell your supervisor straight away. A broken guard, a leaking pipe or a loose ladder can hurt someone tomorrow. The Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993 says workers must report unsafe things and must work safely. Reporting is not getting someone into trouble. It is keeping everyone safe.

Safety signs

Learn the signs. Red signs often mean "stop" or "do not". Blue signs tell you what you must wear. Yellow signs warn of danger. Green signs show first aid and emergency exits.

lessons.title: Security risks
lessons.html:
What is security?

Security means keeping people, grain, machines and money safe from theft, damage and crime. Farms and silos have valuable things: grain, fuel, fertiliser, tools, batteries, cattle and cables. Criminals know this.

Signs of a security risk

  • A gate or door left open or unlocked.
  • A broken fence or a hole under the fence.
  • Strangers walking around without a visitor's badge.
  • A vehicle parked where it should not be, especially at night.
  • Missing tools, fuel or bags.
  • Broken locks or lights that do not work.

What you can do

  1. Lock gates, doors and stores when you leave them.
  2. Do not lend keys to anyone without permission.
  3. Ask strangers politely who they are looking for, and take them to the office or security. Do not fight with anyone.
  4. Do not tell people outside work when cash, fuel or grain is being moved.
  5. Report anything strange to your supervisor or security.

Your own safety comes first

If you see a crime happening, do not try to stop it yourself. Go to a safe place. Call security, your supervisor or the police on 10111. Remember what you saw: how many people, what they wore, the vehicle and its number plate.

Stock theft

On farms with animals, check fences and count animals often. Report missing animals quickly. Fast reporting helps the police find stolen livestock.

Honesty

Taking things from work, even small things like a bag of grain or some diesel, is theft. It can cost you your job and lead to a criminal case.

lessons.title: Environmental risks
lessons.html:
What is the environment?

The environment is the land, water, air, plants and animals around us. Work on farms and at silos can harm the environment if we are careless. We all need clean water, healthy soil and clean air.

Environmental risks at work

RiskWhat to do
Diesel or oil spillsStop the leak if safe, use sand or absorbent, tell your supervisor
Chemical spillsKeep people away, do not touch, report at once
Washing sprayers near a river or damNever do it; use the proper wash area
Rubbish and plasticPut it in the right bin; do not burn plastic
Empty chemical containersNever use them for water or food; return them as the site rules say
Veld firesNo fires or smoking in the veld; report smoke at once
Grain dust and waste grainClean up; waste grain brings rats and birds

Water

Water is precious in South Africa. Close taps. Report leaks. Never let oil, chemicals or dirty water run into a river, dam or borehole. The National Water Act 36 of 1998 protects water resources.

Soil

Do not let fuel or chemicals soak into the soil. Keep vehicles on roads so soil does not get hard and bare.

Fire

In winter the veld is dry. A small spark can start a big fire. Know where the fire beaters and extinguishers are, and know the emergency number for your farm or site.

Key points

  • Look for hazards and report them straight away.
  • Keep away from moving machines and never enter a bin without permission.
  • Lock up and report strangers or damage; do not fight criminals.
  • Clean up spills and keep chemicals out of water and soil.
  • No fires or smoking in dry veld.
